scope.summary: Seed and prove archetypes ARCH-B and ARCH-C per Section 13.27 acceptance archetypes: ARCH-B — extreme-large fake/plastic round implant look on a slender frame (the bolt-on aesthetic as a designed, first-class target per OBR-001); ARCH-C — small perky athletic build; both decouple-proof with firmness-driven soft-tissue divergence.
acceptance_criteria: BRC-ARCH-B sets breast channels to extreme volume + implant-rigid firmness + round/hemispherical shape profile + high upper-pole fullness on slender frame channels; the result reads as the intended fake/plastic bolt-on look — a designed target, not a stacking artifact (OBR-001 verbatim requirement).
BRC-ARCH-C sets small breast volume + perky ptosis on athletic muscle mass/definition channels.
Both archetypes pass BODY_DECOUPLE_VALID; ARCH-B's slender frame channels are bit-identical to their pre-breast-dial values.

Soft-tissue parameters derived from the firmness channel differ mechanically between ARCH-B (implant-rigid motion) and ARCH-C (natural motion) per the MT-539 link — asserted on the derived physics params, proving firmness is a physical channel, not a render label.
Both recipes are deterministic and registered in the QA iterator.
scope.risk_if_missed: The 'everything in between' breast-space claim collapses to one look: the implant aesthetic renders as an accident instead of a target, and firmness stays cosmetic — both explicit operator requirements silently unmet.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
